Recipes will tell you what spices to use for what sort of cuisine you are cooking. Spices like cumin, paprika, ginger and garlic are used in many different dishes and are always good to have on hand. Find a recipe you want to try and get the spices you need it will be well worth it.
You put them in food, then you eat it.

The only advice I can give you is to regularly taste what you're cooking. If you find a recipe and you need to change the servings (recipe serves 8, you want to make it for 16), the spices usually cannot be multiplied like the amount of meat or veggies. So you wouldn't just double the spice, because it could be overpowering and ruin the dish.

Anyway, if you periodically taste what you're cooking before it's finished, you can adjust the spices to your personal preference. It will also help in the future, when you want to cook without a recipe, because you'll have a better understanding of what spice combos work and the ratios you prefer, and you can start creating your own dishes.
